permutationLabel: Base case — painless obstructive jaundice with Courvoisier gallbladder, weight loss and new-onset diabetes
summary: 68-year-old man with 3 weeks of painless jaundice, pruritus, pale stools, 8 kg weight loss and diabetes diagnosed 4 months ago; palpable non-tender gallbladder; bilirubin 236, ALP 690; ultrasound: double-duct dilatation to a 3 cm hypoechoic pancreatic head lesion.

inputs.hpi: Three weeks of yellow skin and eyes without pain, with generalised itching, dark urine and pale stools. Lost 8 kg over three months with poor appetite. Diabetes diagnosed four months ago (HbA1c 7.4%), no family history. Vague dull ache in the upper back at night. No fever or rigors.

exam.general: Deeply jaundiced with scratch marks. Cachectic. Afebrile, pulse 80/min, BP 132/78.
exam.abdomen: Palpable, smooth, non-tender gallbladder in the right upper quadrant (Courvoisier's sign). No hepatomegaly, no ascites.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Dilated intra- and extrahepatic ducts; CBD 14 mm tapering abruptly at the pancreatic head, where there is a 3 cm hypoechoic lesion. Pancreatic duct 5 mm (double-duct sign). Distended gallbladder without stones. No liver lesions seen.

inputs.socialHistory: Retired civil servant. Ex-smoker 30 pack-years. Alcohol occasionally.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma with malignant distal biliary obstruction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Painless obstructive jaundice with Courvoisier gallbladder, weight loss and new-onset diabetes: suspected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (double-duct sign). Needs pancreas-protocol CT staging and HPB MDT.

mustNotMiss.note: Other malignant causes of distal biliary obstruction.

emergencyLevel.note: NICE NG12: jaundice at ≥40 → suspected cancer pathway referral. Must not be routine. iOS (predicted, not observed): urgent ("jaundice" in the CC).

redFlags.note: Painless jaundice, weight loss, new diabetes and a Courvoisier gallbladder.

mustInclude.note: NICE NG85: pancreatic-protocol CT for obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer — before any stent.

mustInclude.note: Specialist pancreatic MDT via the suspected cancer pathway.

mustExclude.note: Routine pre-operative biliary drainage increases complications (DROP); reserve it for cholangitis, delayed surgery or neoadjuvant therapy.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (pancreatic cancer)
guideline.section: Suspected cancer pathway referral for pancreatic cancer at age ≥40 with jaundice; urgent direct-access CT (within 2 weeks) at age ≥60 with weight loss and any of diarrhoea, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation or new-onset diabetes
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG12, June 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: NICE NG85 — Pancreatic cancer in adults: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Pancreatic-protocol CT for obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer; EUS with tissue sampling if unclear; specialist pancreatic MDT; pre-operative biliary drainage only when surgery is delayed, for cholangitis, or before neoadjuvant therapy; SEMS for palliative biliary drainage
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG85, February 2018.

guideline.name: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline — pancreatic cancer
guideline.section: Staging with pancreas-protocol CT (chest/abdomen/pelvis); CA 19-9; MDT resectability assessment; best supportive care and palliation in metastatic disease
guideline.citation: Conroy T, Pfeiffer P, Vilgrain V, et al. Ann Oncol. 2023;34:987–1002.

guideline.name: ESGE Clinical Guideline — endoscopic biliary stenting: indications, choice of stents and results
guideline.section: Self-expanding metal stents for palliation of malignant extrahepatic biliary obstruction; routine pre-operative drainage not recommended
guideline.citation: Dumonceau JM, Tringali A, Papanikolaou IS, et al. Endoscopy. 2018;50:910–930.

guideline.name: DROP trial — preoperative biliary drainage for cancer of the head of the pancreas
guideline.section: Routine preoperative biliary drainage increased serious complications (74% vs 39%) compared with early surgery
guideline.citation: van der Gaag NA, Rauws EAJ, van Eijck CHJ, et al. N Engl J Med. 2010;362:129–137.

rationale: Base case for painless obstructive jaundice: the classic malignant picture (Courvoisier, weight loss, new diabetes, double-duct sign). Tests that the engines rank pancreatic cancer, flag malignancy, keep it off the routine pathway, and order a pancreas-protocol CT and MDT referral before any stent.
